section_summary: Most of this section documents the State Department’s 1937 efforts to obtain photographs of U.S. presidents and Judge Elbert H. Gary for K. Obata’s biography of Viscount Shibusawa, including the search for a missing 1936 despatch, requests to the National Archives and Library of Congress, and correspondence with James A. Farrell. It concludes with the return of borrowed Gary photographs, a 1947 file charge slip, and two 1932 records concerning General Baron Yoshinori Shirakawa’s death after the Hongkew bombing.

subfiles.title: Telegram requesting a duplicate of Tokyo despatch No. 2059
subfiles.to: American Consul, Shanghai, for the American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Department asks the Embassy to provide a duplicate of its missing September 28, 1936 despatch.
subfiles.summary: The Department states that it cannot locate Tokyo despatch No. 2059 of September 28, 1936. It instructs the consul at Shanghai to forward a request by mail to the Embassy in Tokyo for a duplicate copy.

subfiles.title: Telegram asking Dooman what action was taken on the Shibusawa request
subfiles.about: The Department asks Dooman to recall whether any action was taken on the missing despatch.
subfiles.summary: A copy of despatch No. 2059 has arrived, but the Department still cannot find the original or any record of action. The Embassy is asked to have Dooman telegraph what he remembers about its handling.

subfiles.title: Memorandum tracing the proposed reply to despatch No. 2059
subfiles.about: The memorandum records Mrs. Bacon’s recollection of the lost draft response to the Shibusawa biographers’ request.
subfiles.summary: Mrs. Bacon recalled that Mr. Cooke drafted a reply declining Department assistance, but Far Eastern Affairs preferred to offer whatever help was possible. The draft was not returned for revision, and Mrs. Bacon later asked that Mr. Duvall investigate. She never learned what final action was taken and was unsure whether the retained copy had been destroyed.

subfiles.title: Inventory and analysis of the Shibusawa file
subfiles.about: The memorandum inventories records concerning the current photographic request and earlier Shibusawa memorial matters.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum lists the 1936–1937 despatches, telegrams, and internal memoranda concerning photographs requested by Shibusawa’s biographers. It notes Dooman’s recollection that he recommended an informal effort to obtain the photographs and JWB’s report that the original despatch could not be found. Earlier files on condolences after Shibusawa’s death and a memorial presented to President Hoover are declared unrelated to the present case.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram reporting Dooman’s recollection
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports Dooman’s recollection that he recommended seeking the requested photographs informally.
subfiles.summary: Dooman remembered seeing the original despatch with a Protocol Division draft stating that the Department did not normally comply with such requests. He returned the file with the suggestion that the special circumstances justified an effort through informal channels.

subfiles.title: Telegram announcing that photographs will be sent
subfiles.about: The Department informs the Embassy that copies of the requested photographs will go in the next pouch.
subfiles.summary: Referring to despatch No. 2059, the Department states that copies of photographs are being sent to Tokyo in the next pouch. The message closes the immediate effort to locate the initial set of requested images.

subfiles.title: Instruction No. 1307 enclosing four photographs
subfiles.about: The Department sends photographs of three presidents and Judge Gary for use in the Shibusawa biography.
subfiles.summary: The instruction encloses photographs of Presidents Grant, Theodore Roosevelt, and Taft and Judge Gary for K. Obata’s use. It directs the Embassy to explain that future requests of this kind should normally be handled through commercial suppliers, although the Department may provide names of suitable firms.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck’s request to the Archivist of the United States
subfiles.about: Hornbeck asks whether the National Archives can supply photographs of Grant, Theodore Roosevelt, and Taft.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck explains that a Japanese publicist preparing a biography of Viscount Shibusawa needs photographs of three former presidents. Although the Department does not ordinarily undertake such work, special circumstances make it willing to help. He asks the Archivist to search urgently for duplicate prints or suggest another source.

subfiles.title: Archivist’s reply concerning presidential photographs
subfiles.about: The Archivist reports that the National Archives lacks the requested photographs and recommends other sources.
subfiles.summary: Connor states that the Archives has no photographs of Grant, Theodore Roosevelt, or Taft available for the request. He suggests approaching their families or Washington photographers and notes that a Grant image might be copied from the portrait at the White House.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck’s request to the Librarian of Congress
subfiles.about: Hornbeck asks the Library of Congress for duplicate photographs of Grant, Theodore Roosevelt, and Taft.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck describes the Embassy request made on behalf of a Japanese publicist preparing Shibusawa’s biography. Citing special circumstances and urgency, he asks whether the Library can supply duplicate presidential photographs or recommend another source.

subfiles.title: Library of Congress reply identifying commercial photograph sources
subfiles.from: S. G. Caton, Acting Secretary of the Library of Congress
subfiles.about: The Library reports that it lacks duplicate photographs but identifies three Washington suppliers.
subfiles.summary: After consultation with Dr. Holland, the Library states that it has no duplicate photographs of Grant, Theodore Roosevelt, or Taft. It recommends Handy Studios, Haskin’s Information Bureau, and Harris & Ewing, giving addresses and prices for suitable prints or portrait booklets.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck’s request to James A. Farrell for a photograph of Judge Gary
subfiles.about: Hornbeck asks Farrell to supply or help obtain a photograph of Judge Gary.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck explains that the Department is assisting a Japanese publicist preparing a biography of Viscount Shibusawa. He asks Farrell whether he can urgently provide an extra photograph of Judge Gary or suggest another source.

subfiles.title: Farrell’s promise to obtain a Judge Gary photograph
subfiles.about: Farrell agrees to obtain a photograph of Judge Gary and recalls Shibusawa’s interest in Japanese-American friendship.
subfiles.summary: Returning from abroad, Farrell promises to secure a photograph of Judge Gary taken shortly after Gary’s visit to Japan. He recalls meeting Shibusawa during several American visits, including a tour of United States Steel plants. Farrell praises Shibusawa’s interest in friendly relations between Japan and the United States and anticipates the biography with interest.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck’s reply declining further help from Farrell
subfiles.about: Hornbeck thanks Farrell but says that a satisfactory photograph of Judge Gary has already been obtained.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck acknowledges Farrell’s offer to secure a photograph. He explains that the Department has already obtained what appears to be a good copy, so Farrell need not trouble himself further. He adds that the Department looks forward to the Shibusawa biography.

subfiles.title: Farrell’s letter enclosing Gary and Shibusawa photographs
subfiles.about: Farrell sends three borrowed photographic items obtained from Fred R. Sites for transmission to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Farrell reports that Fred R. Sites, who accompanied Judge Gary to Japan, supplied three photographic items. They show Shibusawa’s September 5, 1916 luncheon for Gary, Shibusawa and Gary together, Ōkuma and Gary on the reverse of one card, and a studio portrait of Gary. Because the originals belong to Gary’s former secretary, Farrell asks that they be returned after use.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Farrell’s loaned photographs
subfiles.about: Hornbeck acknowledges the three photographs and promises to send them to Tokyo as a returnable loan.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck thanks Farrell for obtaining the three photographs. He states that they will be forwarded to the American Embassy in Tokyo with instructions that they are loaned for the biography and must be returned through the Department.

subfiles.title: Instruction No. 1333 forwarding the Gary photographs
subfiles.about: The Department forwards the borrowed Gary photographs and directs K. Obata to return them after copying or use.
subfiles.summary: The instruction identifies James A. Farrell and Fred R. Sites as the sources of the photographic materials. It describes the Shibusawa-Gary luncheon images, the Ōkuma-Gary image, and Gary’s studio portrait. Because the items are on loan, the Embassy must have Mr. Obata return them through official channels.

subfiles.title: File copy of Embassy despatch No. 2638 returning photographs
subfiles.about: The Embassy returns the Gary photographs after Obata copied them for the Shibusawa biography.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy returns the photographic materials received with instruction No. 1333 and conveys its thanks and those of K. Obata. Obata made copies and expressed appreciation to everyone who assisted. The enclosure list identifies the luncheon group, paired portraits of Shibusawa, Ōkuma, and Gary, and Gary’s studio portrait.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch No. 2638 returning photographs
subfiles.about: The received copy of the Embassy despatch formally returns the borrowed Gary photographs.
subfiles.summary: Coville reports that Obata has copied the photographs and that the complete set is being returned to the Department. He conveys the gratitude of the Embassy and the biographer. Four images are listed, although two are mounted on opposite sides of one card.

subfiles.title: Hamilton’s letter returning the photographs to Farrell
subfiles.about: Hamilton returns the three borrowed photographic items and conveys the appreciation of the Embassy, Obata, and the Department.
subfiles.summary: Writing while Hornbeck is in Brussels, Hamilton returns the photographs Farrell had sent on August 30. He transmits the thanks of the Tokyo Embassy and the Japanese biographer and adds the Department’s appreciation. The enclosure list describes the Shibusawa-Gary card with the Ōkuma-Gary image on its reverse, the luncheon group, and Gary’s studio portrait.

subfiles.title: Department of State file charge slip
subfiles.about: The slip records the charging of file No. 893.4 to Pratt.
subfiles.summary: This administrative form records a file charge dated May 9, 1947. The listed charge name is QE-Pratt, with additional clerk or location notations.

subfiles.title: Telegram reporting General Shirakawa’s death
subfiles.about: Cunningham reports that the Japanese consul general has confirmed General Shirakawa’s death.
subfiles.summary: Referring to his telegram of May 24, Cunningham states that the Japanese consul general has just informed him that General Shirakawa died at noon. The message was repeated to the Legation.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for the death of General Baron Yoshinori Shirakawa
subfiles.about: The sheet cross-references a record concerning Shirakawa’s death from the Hongkew bombing to file 894.00-P.R./54.
subfiles.summary: The document-file note concerns the death of General Baron Yoshinori Shirakawa as a result of the Hongkew bombing incident. It directs researchers from the Shirakawa personality file to record 894.00-P.R./54.
